title: Bezout component on a finite intersection
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $K,C$ abelian sheaves, $\iota:K\to C$ a morphism, and $C\simeq\underline{\mathbb Z}$ an isomorphism to the constant integer sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Fix finitely many opens $A_i$, natural labels $c_i$, and maps $f_i:j_{A_i!}\underline{\mathbb Z}\to K$ [def-sc-abelian-open-extension-by-zero], each sending its canonical unit to a section whose image in the constant sheaf is $c_i$. For every finite subset $S$ of the indices put $W=\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i$ and $d=\gcd(c_i:i\in S)$, with $W=X$ and $d=0$ for $S=\varnothing$. There is a map $q:j_{W!}\underline{\mathbb Z}\to K$ whose canonical unit has image the constant section $d$. No monicity, positivity, compactness or epimorphism is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 0A38, first two proof paragraphs; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A38

proof.text: Evaluate f_i on its unit and restrict to W for i in S. Naturality of iota followed by isoC and of the sheafification unit shows that each restricted section maps to the constant c_i.

Induct over finite subsets T of S, keeping the ambient open W fixed. The empty subset uses the zero section. On inserting i, combine the section with constant gcd(T) and the restricted section with constant c_i using Nat.gcdA and Nat.gcdB. Mathlib Nat.gcd_eq_gcd_ab, together with additivity and integer scalar compatibility, proves that the new section has constant image gcd(c_i,gcd(T)), which is the finset gcd after insertion.

Apply the already proved private integerExtension_of_section from Sheaf.Topology.ConstantSubsheafQuotientGluing through a proof-only import all. This realizes any given section on W by an integer extension component. Its equation for V=W, followed by the identity restriction map, proves the required unit-value equation. Only this generic helper is used; the quotient-gluing conclusion is not invoked.
